Robert Treat Paine writes to Maryland. Congress deeply feels the manufacture of saltpeter and gunpowder are essential to the safety, freedom and wealth of the United Colonies. Please erect public works and encourage the teaching of the skills necessary in the manufacture of these goods. When we consider how useful saltpeter is, it surely will be taken up by true Americans. Same with gunpowder. Sulphur is found in many Colonies it is supposed. Please take it upon yourselves to earnestly manufacture all possible, and keep Congress informed from time to time of the quantity and state of saltpeter manufacturing, and of gunpowder mills, sulphur mines. Paine closes with solemn words. It is hoped Congress' recommendations are heeded, or else "...it will long be said of us, that we are become Slaves because we were not industrious enough to be free."

John Hancock writes to Thomas Dewees, Prisoner Chief. Please separate into different quarters, certain individuals who are plotting escape. Further, no person is allowed to visit or converse with these individuals.

John Hancock writes to New Jersey Committee of Safety. Folks, we got your communications to Congress, nevertheless you are ordered to immediately march your troops to New York.

Richard Smith recounts Continental Congress. New Jersey raised 4 Companies, and NJ Militia are marching to New York or Staten Island. Tory prisoners in Philadelphia attempted escape, prisoners confined. Money advanced to Commissaries Mease and Fairlamb. Voted down was a proposition to have a Dep. Commisary General established in Virginia. Dugan in Canada is promoted. Morris moved to purchase another ship on behalf of the Continent. A petition for redress was left tabled.

William Whipple writes to Josiah Bartlett. Just returning from Gov. Ward's funeral. He leaves big shoes to fill. Mr. Stilman delivered an excellent sermon. Not sure if it's safe to ship flour - pirates are infesting the coast. A 40 gun ship is reported, and The Lexington has set sail. Our fleet is reported to be at South Carolina but who knows? If you visit Boston please let me know what you see there. Whipple has not received word of New Hampshire in quite a long time. He recommends Bartlett settles his affairs and prepares for the British to return by mid-April.
